summary.text: Natalie Richoz, a registered nurse and write-in independent candidate, lost the November 3, 2026 election for Georgia's 11th Congressional District to John Cowan.
Born in Marietta, she says she has lived in the district for more than 50 years and is a brain-tumor survivor.

paragraphs.text: Richoz was born in Marietta, Georgia. Ballotpedia lists a diploma from Cass High School, a degree from Chattahoochee Technical College in 2006, and an associate degree from Georgia Highlands College in 2010.
Her career experience listed on Ballotpedia includes work as a registered nurse, construction assistant, food service assistant and retail employee.
She describes herself as a wife, mother and grandmother who completed nursing school to earn an RN, and says she has lived in north Georgia's District 11 for more than 50 years.

Richoz is now disabled after surviving a brain tumor that required surgery and radiation treatment, and she says the experience gave her a first-hand view of healthcare from both the provider and patient perspectives.
She was a write-in independent candidate in the November 3, 2026 general election.
During the campaign, she emphasized healthcare reform and protecting Social Security, veterans' benefits, and Medicare and Medicaid.
She lost to John Cowan, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
